alternatives.argument: The definition is locally well-defined: A and B are measurable real random variables, their difference is measurable by closure under finite sums and scalar multiples, and square-integrability of D is an explicit premise ensuring a finite mean and variance. The iid sample plug-in quantities are defined only for n>=2. The full Bland–Altman paper and complete textbook section also directly describe paired differences, signed bias, sample spread, and rounded normal-reference limits.

On the two-point uniform space, E[A]=1/2, E[B]=1/2+c, Var(A)=Var(B)=1/4, and Cov(A,B)=1/4 by the finite weighted-sum formula and covariance bilinearity. Hence Corr(A,B)=1. Pointwise D=-c, so E[D]=-c, Var(D)=0, and both conventional limits equal -c. This is a complete finite counterexample to correlation implying zero bias or agreement.

Assume AC as required by the published normal-law supplier. The normalized positive even density gives a continuous strictly increasing standard-normal CDF with limits 0 and 1; continuity from below/above supplies the limits, and a change of variable proves symmetry. The intermediate value theorem gives the unique z with Phi(z)=.975 and symmetry gives Phi(-z)=.025. For sigma_D>0, the increasing affine map t->mu_D+sigma_D t carries these quantiles to mu_D+-z sigma_D and the interval mass is .95. For sigma_D=0 the law is the point mass at mu_D, so both lower quantiles equal mu_D and the singleton has mass 1. This supplies the complete proof locally.
